page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.A1.Flex.4-32 is an Arm-based virtual machine instance powered by Ampere Altra processors operating at a sustained clock frequency of 3.0 GHz. The instance is provisioned with 4 dedicated physical cores mapping directly to 4 vCPUs with single-threaded execution, avoiding hyperthreading resource contention. It is configured with 32.0 GB of system memory, yielding an allocation of 8.0 GB of RAM per core.

The hardware configuration features an elevated 1:8 core-to-memory ratio, placing the instance into a memory-optimized operational profile. Architectural isolation is reinforced by dedicated per-core hardware assignments, ensuring predictable execution latency across sustained computing tasks. The server contains no integrated local NVMe storage and lacks hardware accelerators, relying entirely on remote block volumes for persistent filesystem needs.

From an efficiency standpoint, the Ampere Altra platform offers high core density and power efficiency compared to traditional x86 alternatives. Because the instance provides substantial memory density per core without incurring GPU overhead, it remains a resource-efficient choice for memory-bound services. However, deployments requiring specialized x86 instruction sets, hardware matrix acceleration, or high local disk IOPS will experience architectural limitations.

VM.Standard.A1.Flex.4-32 is appropriate for in-memory caching layers such as Redis or Memcached, relational databases with moderate query concurrency, mid-sized application servers, containerized microservices, and continuous integration pipelines targeted at 64-bit Arm architectures.
description: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.A1.Flex.4-32 is an Arm-based instance built on the Ampere Altra platform running at a constant 3.0 GHz. The instance allocates 4 dedicated physical cores without simultaneous multithreading, providing 4 vCPUs alongside 32.0 GB of system RAM. With an 8.0 GB per-core allocation, it provides a high memory-to-vCPU ratio suited for memory-intensive computing. The instance lacks local storage devices and discrete GPU accelerators, utilizing remote block storage for persistence and including one complimentary public IPv4 address. Its dedicated core topology avoids hyperthreaded cross-talk, delivering consistent compute performance. VM.Standard.A1.Flex.4-32 is well aligned with memory-bound workloads, including distributed caching systems, relational databases, backend application servers, and native 64-bit Arm software build environments.
